edit.description: The disclosure's two halves disagree. `check` (:54) sums `total` off `member_counts` alone (:71) while `kind_count` (:95) counts `all_kinds` — the union WITH `nested_member_counts` — so the one line that states what was checked undercounts by every embedded member it then enumerates: this repo reads `checked 18 members across 17 kinds: ... handler (6 embedded), hook (6), ... rule (9) ...`, an enumeration summing to 24. Those six handler members are checked — `gate.rs`:453 folds the composed contributor into the corpus the embedded dispatcher judges, and `handlerDefaultContract`'s six clauses fire on them — so the understatement is a disclosure representing less than the run was given (`intent.md`, invariant 6), not a narrower definition of `member`. Fix at the total: sum both maps, so the sentence's count and its enumeration are one fact. Stale prose rides this edit — the doc at :34-:35 calls `nested_member_counts` "the per-kind embedded-member count grouped from the lock's nested_member rows", one of the two sources `gate.rs`:766-772 now folds in.

`an_embedded_kind_with_nested_members_renders_a_nonzero_embedded_marked_count` (:219) is the exact twin and the reason the gap shipped: it pins the per-kind marker (`supporting-doc (1 embedded)`, :259) and never the headline, so its own fixture — a skill on disk plus one `nested_member` row — discloses `checked 1 member` over two checked members and passes. Extend it, or add its sibling, asserting the total counts the embedded member too, with the non-vacuity pin that the embedded set was populated (`engineering.md`, "A green verdict is proven non-vacuous").
